decision: cloud threads: create sessions through a routine's documented API trigger (POST /v1/claude_code/routines/<trig>/fire, returns claude_code_session_id); send follow-ups with claude -p msg --cloud <id>
why: claude -p --cloud <task> is rejected: 'Starting a new cloud session with --cloud is interactive only'; the fire token is made for machine callers, so the DO can hold it

decision: MCP tools reach cloud sessions as a claude.ai connector, not a repo .mcp.json
why: connector traffic goes through Anthropic's servers and skips the environment's network allowlist; no file in each repo

decision: live probe blocked: this machine's Claude CLI authenticates with apiKeyHelper through cli.maximilion.ai, so cloud create fails with fetchEnvironments 403
why: cloud sessions need a claude.ai sign-in; changing auth is Max's call

decision: pnpm live runs the local chain on OpenRouter deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash; e2e and live share scripts/stack.ts
why: first real-model turns: clone, list, read, write, typecheck, end_turn in 4.3 s and 4.1 s

decision: tools accept ./ prefixes and . for the workspace root
why: the first real turn failed list_files . with the RelativePath error; scripted test fails without the fix, passes with it; rerun of the real prompt lists . fine

decision: 100 concurrent sessions on the local stack: 100/100 end_turn with a clean typecheck, p50 7.2 s, max 15.7 s; peak RSS nc 2.8 MB each, acp-mux +44 MB, workerd +350 MB for 200 DOs, typecheck +23 MB and 1.2 CPU-s for 100 checks
why: measure before claiming the 100-thread goal; local workerd keeps every DO in one process, so this is not Cloudflare billing

decision: OpenCode runs as a second agent loop behind HARNESS (pi default, opencode); a session records its loop and keeps it
why: agents@0.31 ships OpenCodeHarness on workerd; the ACP surface, tools, guards, typecheck, history and retention stay shared

decision: our tools replace every OpenCode tool, Code Mode is denied, title calls are off
why: OpenCode's workerd profile stubs its filesystem and shell, but webfetch reached the network when its tools were left in (mutation run: 502 GET http://attacker.test/)
evidence: test/opencode.test.ts: offers the model none of OpenCode's own tools

decision: pin @opencode/* 2.2.3 with an exact-version minimumReleaseAgeExclude
why: 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 run OpenCode's npm provider installer before plugin AI SDK hooks (DynamicProviderPlugin in pre); 2.2.3 moved it to post, so plugin models load on workerd
evidence: bead t3-code-dorbs-mcd drops the exclusion after 2026-10-31T09:51Z

decision: each AcpSession gets its own OpenCode session id, not the harness root ses_root
why: OpenCode keys a per-isolate inbox mutex by session id; DOs sharing an isolate deadlocked on ses_root (AsyncLocalStorage bound function called outside its request)
evidence: test/opencode.test.ts: runs prompts of sessions that share an isolate at the same time (fails on ses_root)

decision: import OpenCode on an OpenCode session's first prompt
why: wrangler check startup, local CPU: 57 ms script before OpenCode, 139 ms with a static import, 64 ms with the dynamic one; bundle 0.86 MB to 4.58 MB gzip either way

decision: pi vs opencode, 10 sessions at once, local stack: scripted p50 207 vs 1305 ms, workerd CPU 0.029 vs 0.188 s/session, RSS 292 vs 436 MB, SQLite 296 vs 468 KB/session; DeepSeek 10/10 vs 10/10, p50 5.8 vs 8.5 s, max 21.6 vs 9.0 s, CPU 0.14 vs 0.34 s/session
why: measure before choosing; one earlier OpenCode DeepSeek run got 3/10 while another project's workerd and a vitest run loaded the machine, not reproduced in three runs since

decision: a prompt sent while a turn runs waits for that turn instead of failing with -32600 (t3-code-dorbs-561)
why: T3 sends the user's next prompt right after session/load and has no way to see that a turn still runs (ACP v1 load has no running state); an error loses the prompt, a wait runs it after the orphaned turn; a cancel answers waiting prompts as cancelled so stop still stops everything
evidence: test/acp.test.ts: runs a prompt sent while a turn runs; test/restart.test.ts: shows a turn still running to a client that reconnects

decision: open prompts live in AcpSession storage and a restarted session runs the first one on as the same operation id (t3-code-dorbs-bls)
why: pi-durable resets running tasks to pending on open and reruns them (scheduler.js:195), replay-safe tools rerun, others settle as interrupted (tool.js:119-131), a partial answer becomes an aborted entry (generation.js:304-312), 5 restarts without progress park a task (agent.js:35); PiHarness wake job restarts the object within a 30 s heartbeat (agents harness/pi/index.js:38)

decision: OpenCode: on rejoin catch up from session.log() from the operation's inbox.enqueued, skipping keys already sent (tool start/end, ended text parts) kept in opencode/published (t3-code-dorbs-x8f)
why: OpenCode resumes a cut-off turn while it boots, before events() attaches, and can finish it unwatched; it adds a synthetic 'server restarted' user message and gives up after 10 resumes with Execution.Failed (@opencode/core session/execution/restart.js:262-294)
evidence: test/opencode.test.ts: catches up from OpenCode's durable log; fails without the catch-up

decision: the thread says '(Restarted; resuming this turn.)' where a cut-off turn picks up
why: both loops redo the step a restart cut off, so T3 would join the pre-restart partial and the new answer into one garbled message
evidence: test/restart.test.ts: middle of a model stream

decision: restart tests warm the lazily imported tool modules in beforeAll
why: the vitest pool fetches a dynamic import over the module runner; aborting the object mid-fetch leaves @cloudflare/computer's diff import (git.js:3915) pending for good, which the Worker bundle (in-memory chunks) never hits
evidence: probe: same restart passes once the module is warm
